text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Tuesday in anticipation of a low consumer price index, the prime minister's call for lower interest rates and expectations of progress in talks with the Palestinians, traders said.
* CPI (consumer price index) linked government bonds: +0.1 pct to 167.91
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.1 pct to 166.40
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: unchanged at 158.01
"The market is very volatile and any excuse can be used to explain the rises today," said Miron Katzap of Batucha Securities.
"There were rises across the board while dollar-linked bonds were unchanged," he said.

"The rises today were a correction to the price falls registered last week in the CPI-linked bonds, but also a reaction to the prime minister's call for lower interest rates, to the progress in the peace process and in expectation of a low CPI," said an investment manager.
September's CPI, released after the end of the trading day, rose 0.4 percent, the same level as in August.
"There is a feeling that the market is stabilising around the current yields," the investment manager said.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu broke ranks with central bank governor Jacob Frenkel on Monday and called for a cut in interest rates at a meeting with business leaders and government officials. Traders have said the high-interest rate policies of the Bank of Israel are hurting the capital markets.

Israel and the Palestinian Authority started intensive negotiations last week towards implementing a deal to redeploy Israeli troops in the West Bank town of Hebron, signed by Israel's previous government.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
